solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Volunteers shown disrespect? That's forbidden

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
an audience that boos a performer shows disrespect, so the performer was booed

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether jeering at volunteers is off-limits, and is told it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is the British Army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden has been placed under a taboo, a social or religious prohibition.

clue.text: Provoker of controversy rising up, outwardly aloof

indicators.note: outwardly means the word for aloof sits on the outside, wrapping the other piece

parts.note: someone aloof is distant and reserved

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word up is read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A stand-offish troublemaker gets worked up while keeping a cool exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue 'rising' makes PU, and 'outwardly' has the aloof word wrapped round it.
explanation.definitionFit: A disputant is one who argues, so is a person who stirs up or engages in controversy.

clue.text: Stranger more boozed up, losing head

indicators.note: losing head tells us to drop the first letter of the word for more boozed up

parts.note: beerier means more affected by beer, more drunk

explanation.surface: An oddball becomes even more tipsy and starts losing control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes the B off BEERIER. 'Stranger' looks like a noun for an unknown person, but here it is the comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are comparatives: eerier means more weird or uncanny, that is, odder in an unsettling way.

clue.text: Very obscene beast running fast to grab daughter — gosh!

indicators.note: to grab means the animal's name takes hold of the following letters inside itself

parts.note: a hare is a fast-running animal
cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like gosh

explanation.surface: A sprinting animal seizes a girl, and an onlooker exclaims in shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gosh' is matched by a British exclamation of surprise; 'to grab' makes the animal hold both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardcore describes the most explicit kind of pornography, so it means extremely obscene.

clue.text: Lack the ability to take the right steps, evidently!

definitions.text: Lack the ability to take the right steps, evidently!

parts.words: Lack the ability to take the right steps, evidently!
parts.note: the idiom for being a clumsy dancer, read literally, describes someone who has no right foot at all and so cannot step with the right

explanation.walkthrough: 'Right steps' means correct dance moves, but also steps taken with a right foot, which someone with two left ones literally cannot take.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a clumsy, awkward dancer who cannot move gracefully.

clue.text: King, say, associated with top people who would support his supremacy?

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
eg (for example) means say
the A-list is the set of most celebrated people

explanation.surface: A monarch mixes with celebrities who would back his claim to absolute power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King, say' looks like one unit meaning a monarch as an example, but it splits into R and EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A regalist is a supporter of royal authority, so would back a monarch's supremacy.

clue.text: Island's copper coming down on outlawry

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming down on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a ban is a prohibition, a putting outside the law

explanation.surface: An island policeman cracks down hard on crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' reads as a policeman but gives the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to Cuba, the Caribbean island, matching the possessive form.

clue.text: Triangle struck to set off a fairy dance

indicators.note: struck means the letters of the instrument are knocked into a new order
to set off a means the letter a is put aside from the shuffled letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A percussionist hits the triangle to start the fairies dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struck' rearranges TRIANGLE, and 'to set off a' removes one A from the result. The fairy sense is Shakespearean: Titania's fairies dance their ringlets to the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: In old poetic usage, a ringlet was a circle dance performed by fairies, as in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Boyish girl wanting home in Rugby, maybe

indicators.note: in tells us the word for home goes inside the word for rugby

parts.note: rugby is an example of a game
in means at home

explanation.surface: A tomboyish girl longs to be back home in Rugby, the English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby looks like the Warwickshire town, but it is the sport, an example of a GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamine is a slim girl with an elfin, boyish charm, such as Audrey Hepburn.

clue.text: Very small ruler confronting spy is a scamp

indicators.note: confronting means the ruler faces the spy, standing in front of it

parts.note: an aga was a minor Turkish commander or chief, a petty ruler
James Bond is the fictional spy

explanation.surface: A tiny tyrant facing a secret agent turns out to be a rascal.
explanation.walkthrough: An aga is an Ottoman chief. 'Ruler' could be a measuring stick, but here it is a person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagabond is a rogue or wastrel, close in sense to a scamp or rascal.

clue.text: Grumble with energy, having missed a prayer session

indicators.note: having missed means the letter a is left out of the combined pieces

parts.note: to grumble is to complain
E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles energetically after skipping a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having missed' removes the A that the grumbling word contains, before the energy letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Compline is the last of the canonical hours, the night office of prayers said before bed.

clue.text: Uninhabited city — half of it destroyed, see

indicators.note: half of it destroyed means only the first half of the city's name survives

parts.note: London, the capital, is the city
Ely, a cathedral city, is the seat of a bishop, a see

explanation.surface: A city lies deserted after half of it is wrecked, look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a verb but is a bishop's see: Ely, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A lonely place is remote and unfrequented, with few or no people living there.

clue.text: Long-contested site for development? PM joins argument

parts.note: Edward Heath was the British Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974
a row is a quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister wades into a heated planning dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: Heathrow airport's expansion, notably a third runway, has been fought over for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: London's main airport has been a long-running battleground over plans to expand it.

clue.text: Dated order — only time must be limited

indicators.note: must be limited means the honour's letters enclose the other pieces, bounding them

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire
sole means only, single

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned instruction says only a short time is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' reads as a command, but it is the British honour OBE (Order of the British Empire).
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolete is out of date, no longer in use or fashion.

clue.text: Clumsy feller's job

definitions.meaning: a feller cuts down trees, whose trade is cutting and preparing timber

explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' is not a chap but one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means moving heavily, and also the trade of felling and preparing timber.

clue.text: Rodent quietly hiding in islet upset horse

indicators.note: hiding in means the soft sign is tucked inside the small island

parts.note: a cay is a small low island
P stands for piano, quietly in music

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the horse breed is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A rodent sneaks quietly onto an island and spooks a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue 'upset' turns the horse upside down, giving BARA; 'hiding in' tucks the quiet letter into the islet.
explanation.definitionFit: The capybara of South America is the largest living rodent.

clue.text: Substance in body supporting rib

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
to rib someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Something inside the body props up a rib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rib' looks like a bone, fitting 'body', but it is the verb meaning tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A protease is an enzyme in the body that breaks down proteins.

clue.text: One who designed many a madonna and archangel

definitions.text: One who designed many a madonna
definitions.meaning: the Italian Renaissance painter famous for his many paintings of the Virgin and Child
one of the archangels of tradition, the healer in the Book of Tobit

explanation.walkthrough: 'madonna' may suggest the pop singer, but it is the Virgin Mary in paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the painter Raffaello Sanzio and to an archangel of Jewish and Christian tradition.

clue.text: Oriental garment, very large, with gold lining, housed by university

indicators.note: housed by means the other letters sit inside the university's initials

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

indicators.note: lining means the metal's symbol goes round the size letters, forming a border

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: An outsize Eastern robe, gold-lined, is kept at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lining' puts the gold round the size letters, making AOSU, and 'housed by' places that inside the university. 'lining' is used loosely for an edging here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mao suit is the high-collared tunic suit associated with Chairman Mao and Chinese dress.

clue.text: Ancestor transported food, according to Spooner

indicators.note: according to Spooner signals swapping the opening sounds of the two words, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: bore means carried, transported
fare means food

explanation.surface: An ancestor carried food around, the Reverend Spooner would say.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BORE FARE gives 'fore bare', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is someone from whom one is descended, a forefather.

clue.text: Designation of sea in which sailor is slow

indicators.note: in which means the sailor goes inside the sea's name

parts.note: Red is the name of the Red Sea
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor on a particular sea is slow to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slow' is a verb here: to slow something down.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard something is to delay it or make it go more slowly.

clue.text: Inconsistent agent keeping too much hidden

indicators.note: keeping means the agent holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
OTT is over the top, too much

explanation.surface: A secret agent keeps something excessive under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts 'too much' inside the agent; OTT stands for over the top, a common British abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotty performance is patchy, uneven in quality, so inconsistent.

clue.text: Slim girl's No.1 obsession

parts.note: thin means slim

indicators.note: No.1 means the first letter of girl's

explanation.surface: A slender young woman's chief fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slim girl' looks like one phrase, but Slim is THIN and the girl gives only G.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something is informal for being obsessed with it.

clue.text: One with anticipation of endless enjoyment — traveller missing nothing

indicators.note: endless means the word for enjoyment loses its last letter

parts.note: fun is enjoyment

indicators.note: missing means the zero is dropped from the traveller

parts.note: a tourist is a traveller
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone looking forward to never-ending fun, and a traveller who has forgotten nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: FU (FUN with its end cut off) and TURIST (TOURIST with O for nothing removed) join together.
explanation.definitionFit: A futurist looks ahead and forecasts what is to come, so is someone given to anticipation.

clue.text: Show eagerness maybe, making business transaction without one form of tax

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the sale wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a sale is a business transaction
I is the Roman numeral one
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A deal is done without one kind of tax being added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of outside, so the transaction surrounds one and the tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Drooling, as at the prospect of food, is an example of how eagerness can be shown.

clue.text: Famous artist — there's hesitation about his lack of colour

indicators.note: about means the hesitation sound is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation
noir is French for black, the absence of colour, in the French painter's own language

explanation.surface: A great painter hesitates over going colourless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses ER to RE. 'his' points to the painter's French, in which black is noir.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a celebrated French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: Notorious prisoner in loud tirade

indicators.note: in means the prisoner is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: F is forte, loud in music
a rant is a tirade
lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: An infamous convict delivers a noisy harangue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the prisoner inside the other pieces; an old lag is British slang for a long-serving convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means glaringly obvious, so conspicuously bad, notorious.
